blocks.title: Present perfect vs past simple · B1

items.en: I saw him at the station yesterday.
items.cz: Včera jsem ho viděl na nádraží.
items.gap: I ____ him at the station yesterday. (see)
accepts: I saw him at the station yesterday.
items.explanation: "yesterday" names a finished time, so past simple: saw. Not have seen — that leaves the time open.
items.explanation_cz: „yesterday“ pojmenovává uzavřený čas, proto minulý prostý: saw. Ne have seen — ten nechává čas otevřený.

items.en: I have seen that film before.
accepts: I have seen that film before.
I've seen that film before.
items.explanation: "before" counts experience up to now, so present perfect: have seen. Not saw — no finished time is named.
items.explanation_cz: „before“ počítá zkušenost až do teď, proto předpřítomný: have seen. Ne saw — žádný uzavřený čas tu není.

items.en: He has already left the office.
accepts: He has already left the office.
He's already left the office.
items.explanation: "already" leaves the time open, so present perfect: has left. Not left — that would close it.
items.explanation_cz: „already“ nechává čas otevřený, proto předpřítomný: has left. Ne left — ten by ho uzavřel.

items.en: My parents had lunch at twelve.
accepts: My parents had lunch at twelve.
items.explanation: "at twelve" names a finished time, so past simple: had. Not have had — that leaves the time open.
items.explanation_cz: „at twelve“ pojmenovává uzavřený čas, proto minulý prostý: had. Ne have had — ten nechává čas otevřený.

items.en: My parents have already had lunch.
accepts: My parents have already had lunch.
My parents have had lunch already.
items.explanation: "already" leaves the time open, so present perfect: have had. Not had — that would close it.
items.explanation_cz: „already“ nechává čas otevřený, proto předpřítomný: have had. Ne had — ten by ho uzavřel.

items.en: I sent the tickets last Tuesday.
items.cz: Ty lístky jsem poslal minulé úterý.
accepts: I sent the tickets last Tuesday.
items.explanation: "last Tuesday" names a finished time, so past simple: sent. Not have sent — that leaves the time open.
items.explanation_cz: „last Tuesday“ pojmenovává uzavřený čas, proto minulý prostý: sent. Ne have sent — ten nechává čas otevřený.

items.en: I have just sent the tickets.
accepts: I have just sent the tickets.
I've just sent the tickets.
items.explanation: "just" leaves the time open, so present perfect: have just sent. Not sent — that would close it.
items.explanation_cz: „just“ nechává čas otevřený, proto předpřítomný: have just sent. Ne sent — ten by ho uzavřel.

items.en: Then I moved to a smaller town.
items.cz: Potom jsem se přestěhoval do menšího města.
items.gap: Then I ____ to a smaller town. (move)
accepts: Then I moved to a smaller town.
items.explanation: "Then" walks through finished steps, so past simple: moved. Present perfect cannot follow then.
items.explanation_cz: „Then“ vypráví hotové kroky za sebou, proto minulý prostý: moved. Předpřítomný po then nejde.

items.en: After that he found a new job.
items.gap: After that he ____ a new job. (find)
accepts: After that he found a new job.
items.explanation: "After that" is the next finished step, so past simple: found. Present perfect would break the story line.
items.explanation_cz: „After that“ je další hotový krok, proto minulý prostý: found. Předpřítomný by narušil linku vyprávění.

labels: Same event — we talk about the result now.
points: I **moved** last year. We name **when** the moving happened.
I **have moved**. Same moving — we name what is true **now**.

cards.title: Past simple — when?
points: The **time** of the action is finished — not the whole story.

rows: I **have lost** my keys. (I don’t have them now.)
I **have lived** here for 12 years. (I still do.)

cards.title: Why it matters
points: Listeners hear **then** as a finished step → past simple
Present perfect with **then** often sounds wrong

cards.title: Unfinished time
points: If the story says **then** / **after that**, use past simple.
**for** / **since** with a situation that continues → present perfect.

rows: I ___ (live) here for twelve years. (still here)
